prose:
Gary Marcus comments on Levent Alpöge's reported claim of a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, emphasizing prolonged human guidance and the role of Lean and mathlib rather than a single autonomous answer. He argues that success in a formally checkable mathematical domain would not, by itself, establish general intelligence, dependable business automation or a change in commercial margins.

This is commentary on an apparently claimed result, not a verification or acceptance of a proof. Marcus's descriptions of a 250,000-page artifact, its formal status, the extent of human work and its market reception remain attributed assertions in this pass; no proof artifact, independent review or market data was inspected here. The claim is distinct from the earlier hypothetical interview video and from other claimed-proof PDFs already indexed. Neither the title nor repetition by commentators settles the mathematical result or establishes how much of the work was produced by AI.
highlights: Marcus emphasizes human direction in the reported Claude collaboration
Lean and mathlib are central to his account of formal verification
The claimed Riemann result is not independently verified or accepted here
Artifact length and formal status remain attributed assertions
A result in a checkable domain would not alone establish general intelligence
No market response or enterprise value change was independently checked
Separate commentary from the hypothetical video and other claimed-proof artifacts
